title: Automated testing
summary: Which automated tests a service needs before a release, so that changes can be made often without breaking what customers rely on.
scope: Applications and libraries built by company teams. Bought software is tested by its supplier and is out of scope.

resources.title: Testing handbook
resources.description: What to test at which level, with examples per language.

requirements.title: Tests run before every release
requirements.statement: The automated tests of a service run in the build pipeline on every change, and a release is built only from a commit whose tests passed.
requirements.rationale: Tests that are run by hand are skipped exactly when the deadline is close.
guidance: Add the test command to the shared build workflow.
Do not mark failing tests as skipped to get a release out; fix or remove them in a reviewed change.

lookFor: A test disabled or skipped without a linked ticket
A workflow change that lets a release build run when tests fail

requirements.title: A test with every bug fix
requirements.statement: A pull request that fixes a bug adds a test that fails without the fix.
requirements.rationale: Bugs that come back after a release cost customers' trust twice.
guidance: Write the test first and check that it fails.
Name the test after the behaviour, not the ticket number.

lookFor: A pull request titled or labelled as a fix that changes no test file

requirements.title: End-to-end tests for key customer journeys
requirements.statement: Critical services have automated end-to-end tests for their main customer journeys, run against staging before each release.
requirements.rationale: Unit tests do not show that the services still work together.
guidance: List the three to five journeys that make the money, e.g. sign in, search, pay.
Keep each journey test under two minutes.

verification.description: Checked in the yearly quality review of each critical service.

requirements.title: Contract tests between services
requirements.statement: Services that call each other's APIs may use contract tests to find breaking changes before release.
requirements.rationale: Contract tests find a breaking API change in the pull request instead of in staging.

lookFor: A change to an API response with no change to its contract file
